operation.description: Merge sources[] into this asset as a stack. It links, never moves: each source slot (but its proxy and thumbnail) becomes a destination slot naming the same blobs, with its revision history, and records the source slot it came from; the source rows stay untouched and the source is hidden (404 everywhere, out of every listing) until a split or finalize. Tags are unioned unless union_tags is false, a property the destination lacks is copied, and every addition is recorded so a split takes it back. Refusals: 404 for a missing, hidden, trashed or merged participant; 403 without edit rights, or when the merge would show a source to someone who cannot see it today and the caller is neither that source's owner nor a full admin (reason widening); 409 when a source itself holds active merges (reason nested). See the DAM API details article for errors and lifecycle behavior.

operation.description: Update only name (nullable max 255), no_expiry or expiry_days 1–365, and the link options: password (4–128, sets or changes it), remove_password boolean (clears it; not with password), allow_download, requires_creator_access. no_expiry=true takes precedence. An omitted option is left unchanged. Does not change target. slug (optional, P4 D23): the link's custom address /s/{slug}, 3–64 lowercase letters, digits and single hyphens (input is lowercased), never a reserved word, unique across shares and collections (a slug any link or collection has held stays theirs); 422 otherwise, and a refused slug creates or changes nothing. It is an alias, not a secret: /s/{slug} redirects to the token URL while the link opens, so anyone with it can open the link (its password still applies). slug, slug_url and share_url (the URL to copy: the slug's when set) are shown only beside the token (the link's creator, the target's owner or a full admin), and only they may set it (else 403). A collection's link takes no slug (422). A new slug keeps the old one answering 301 to it; slug null clears it. See the DAM API details article for errors and lifecycle behavior.
